about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Danish Brown-Butter Carrots with Parsley
recipes.summary: Carrot batons glazed in nutty brown butter, honey and lemon.
steps: Put the carrots, water and salt in a wide frying pan, cover and simmer for 8 minutes until the carrots are just tender.
Uncover and boil off the remaining water until the pan is nearly dry.
Add the butter and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the butter foams and smells nutty.
Stir in the honey and lemon juice and toss for 1 minute until the carrots are glossy, then scatter with parsley.
notes: Pairs well with roast chicken, fish or pork.
Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

recipes.title: Swedish Honey-Roasted Swede Wedges
recipes.summary: Sweet, sticky roast swede with thyme, a classic Nordic winter side.

items: 700g swede, peeled and cut into wedges

steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray with baking paper.
Toss the swede with the oil, thyme, salt and pepper and spread in a single layer.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned at the edges.
Drizzle with the honey and roast for 8 minutes more until sticky and caramelised.
notes: Swede can be tough to cut, so slice a flat side first for a stable base.

recipes.title: Danish Sweet-Sour Red Cabbage with Apple
recipes.summary: Slow-braised red cabbage with apple, cinnamon and vinegar, served warm or cold.
steps: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cabbage, apple, cinnamon, sugar, salt and water and stir well.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the cabbage is very tender.
Stir in the vinegar and cook uncovered for 5 minutes until the liquid is syrupy.
notes: Flavour improves overnight; reheat gently.
Freezes well for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Garlic Walnut Paste with Coriander for Roast Vegetables
recipes.summary: A garlicky walnut sauce with coriander and vinegar for roast vegetables, chicken or fish.
steps: Blend the walnuts, garlic, coriander leaves, ground coriander, chilli and salt until a coarse paste forms.
Add the vinegar and water a little at a time and blend until a thick, spoonable sauce forms.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
notes: Keeps in a clean jar in the fridge for 4 days; thin with water if it thickens.
Serve about 2 tablespoons per person.

recipes.title: Warm Green Beans in Garlic Walnut Paste
recipes.summary: Tender green beans in a garlicky walnut and coriander dressing, served warm or at room temperature.
steps: Boil the beans in salted water for 5 minutes until tender but still bright green, then drain.
Blend the walnuts, garlic, vinegar, oil, ground coriander, salt and water until a thick, rough paste forms.
Toss the warm beans with the walnut paste until evenly coated.
Scatter with coriander leaves and serve.
notes: Also good as a cold lunchbox side.

recipes.title: Latvian Grated Carrot Salad with Sour Cream and Sultanas
recipes.summary: A sweet and creamy carrot salad with dill, common on Baltic tables.
steps: Mix the sour cream, lemon juice, dill and salt in a large bowl until smooth.
Fold through the grated carrot and sultanas until evenly coated.
Taste, adjust the lemon and serve cold.
notes: Best eaten within 2 days; the carrot softens as it sits.

recipes.title: Creamy Chilled Avocado Soup with Coriander
recipes.summary: A no-cook blended soup, creamy and bright, for warm days.
steps: Blend the avocado, cucumber, stock, yoghurt, lime juice, spring onion and salt until completely smooth.
Taste and add more lime or salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls and top with coriander.
notes: The colour browns in the air, so serve the same day.
Use cold stock for a properly chilled soup.

recipes.title: Guyanese Split Pea Soup with Flour Spinners
recipes.summary: A hearty yellow split pea soup with thyme, cumin and little rolled flour dumplings.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, garlic and carrot for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cumin and thyme for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the split peas, the 2 litres of water and 1 tsp salt.
Simmer for 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas have broken down into a thick soup.
Mix the flour, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/3 cup water into a firm dough, roll into thin finger-length spinners and drop them into the soup.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the spinners are cooked through and the soup is thick.
notes: Add a splash of water when reheating; the soup thickens as it cools.
Freezes well without the spinners.

recipes.title: Bajan Sweet Potato Soup with Ginger and Coconut
recipes.summary: A velvety orange soup with fresh ginger, coconut milk and a squeeze of lime.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the sweet potato and stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the sweet potato is very soft.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth, stir in the coconut milk and heat for 3 minutes until just steaming.
Finish with the lime juice and season to taste.
notes: Freezes well for up to 3 months without the coconut milk; add it when reheating.

recipes.title: Swedish Dill and Mustard Potato Salad
recipes.summary: Warm waxy potatoes in a tangy mustard and olive oil dressing with red onion and dill, no mayo.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 minutes until a knife slips in easily, then drain.
Whisk the oil, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the warm potatoes and onion and toss gently until coated.
Fold through the dill and serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Travels well in a lunchbox; it does not need keeping cold for a few hours but is best chilled for longer transport.

recipes.title: Turmeric Silverbeet with Ginger, Ethiopian Style
recipes.summary: Silverbeet gently braised with garlic, ginger and turmeric in the style of gomen.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the silverbeet stems, water and salt, cover and cook for 5 minutes until the stems soften.
Add the leaves and cook uncovered for 6 minutes, stirring, until tender and the liquid has cooked off.
notes: Serve with flatbread, lentils or rice.
Silverbeet is naturally salty, so taste before adding more salt.

recipes.title: Ugandan Rolex Egg and Chapati Rolls
recipes.summary: Street-style breakfast rolls of folded omelette, cabbage and tomato in warm flatbread.
steps: Whisk the eggs with the salt and stir through the onion and tomato.
Heat half the oil in a frying pan and cook half the egg mixture for 3 minutes, flipping once, until fully set; repeat with the rest.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side until soft.
Lay an omelette on each flatbread, top with cabbage and roll up tightly.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set with no runny egg, especially for children, older adults or anyone pregnant.
Eat the same day.

recipes.title: Trinidadian Curried Channa Breakfast with Flatbread
recipes.summary: Spiced curried chickpeas with tomato, scooped up with toasted flatbread.
steps: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes until it breaks down.
Add the chickpeas, water and salt and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas, until thick.
Toast the flatbreads in a dry pan until warm and lightly browned, then serve with the channa and coriander.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days and tastes better the next day.

recipes.title: Toasted Sesame and Rice Vinegar Slaw Dressing
recipes.summary: A quick Asian-style dressing for crunchy cabbage and carrot slaw.
steps: Whisk the sesame oil, rice vinegar, soy sauce, honey, ginger and garlic in a bowl until the honey dissolves.
Stir in the sesame seeds and taste, adding a little more vinegar if you like it sharper.
Toss through shredded cabbage, carrot and spring onion just before serving.
notes: Makes enough for about 600g of shredded vegetables.
Keeps in a jar in the fridge for 5 days; shake before using.

recipes.title: Coconut Lime Dressing for Red Cabbage Slaw
recipes.summary: A creamy, tangy dressing with lime, chilli and coriander for slaws and grilled fish.
steps: Whisk the coconut cream, lime juice, honey, oil and salt in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the chilli and coriander and taste, adding more lime or honey to balance.
Toss through shredded red cabbage and carrot just before serving.
notes: Coconut cream firms in the fridge; stir or warm briefly to loosen.
Keeps for 3 days.

recipes.title: Cocoa Oat Smoothie with Peanut Butter
recipes.summary: A filling chocolatey breakfast smoothie with rolled oats and peanut butter.
steps: Put the oats, milk, peanut butter, cocoa, honey and ice in a blender.
Blend on high for 1 minute until completely smooth with no oat flecks.
Pour into two glasses and drink straight away.
notes: Contains peanuts and milk; swap in oat milk and sunflower seed butter if needed.
For a thicker smoothie use less ice.

recipes.title: Gentle Rice and Chicken Soup with Ginger
recipes.summary: A mild soup of poached chicken, soft rice, carrot and ginger, plain and warm.
steps: Bring the stock, water, ginger, carrots and celery to a simmer in a large pot for 5 minutes until the carrots start to soften.
Add the chicken and rice and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the rice is very soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot.
Season with the salt and top with spring onions.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until there is no pink and the juices run clear, with an internal temperature of 75°C.
Food safety: cooked rice should be cooled and refrigerated within 1 hour, and reheated until steaming hot.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Pumpkin and Chicken Soup with Thyme
recipes.summary: A mild, comforting soup of poached chicken and soft pumpkin with thyme and white pepper.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the pumpkin, stock, water, thyme and bay leaf and bring to a simmer for 5 minutes until steaming.
Add the chicken and simmer for 20 minutes until the pumpkin is very soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and shred it, discard the bay leaf, then lightly mash the pumpkin into the broth until thick.
Return the chicken to the pot, season with salt and white pepper and heat for 2 minutes until hot.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until there is no pink and the juices run clear, with an internal temperature of 75°C.
Freezes well for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Budget Cabbage, Potato and White Bean Soup
recipes.summary: A cheap, filling pantry soup that feeds six for very little.

items: 400g can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and carrots for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes, cabbage, water, stock powder and thyme and simmer for 20 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the beans and simmer for 5 minutes until heated through.
Mash a few potato cubes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup and season to taste.
notes: Costs roughly a dollar a serve using supermarket basics.
Freezes well for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Freezer-Batch Tomato and Red Capsicum Soup
recipes.summary: A big batch of smoky roasted-style tomato and capsicum soup that freezes in single portions.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onions and capsicum for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, paprika and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 20 minutes until the capsicum is very soft.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth and season with the salt.
notes: Cool completely before freezing in portions for up to 3 months; reheat until steaming hot.
Leave a gap at the top of each container as the soup expands.

recipes.title: High-Fibre Oat Bran and Apple Breakfast Bowl
recipes.summary: Creamy oat bran porridge topped with grated apple, sunflower seeds and walnuts.
steps: Stir the oat bran, milk and cinnamon in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Spoon into bowls and top with the apple, sunflower seeds and walnuts.
notes: Use any milk you like; the fibre is mostly from the oat bran, apple and sunflower seeds.
Add a splash more milk for a looser porridge.

recipes.title: High-Fibre Black Bean and Corn Breakfast Tostadas
recipes.summary: Crisp corn tortillas with black beans, sweet corn, avocado and a fried egg.

items: 400g can black beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Heat the oven to 200C, brush the tortillas with the olive oil and bake on trays for 8 minutes until crisp and lightly golden.
Warm the beans, corn, cumin and salt in a saucepan for 5 minutes, mashing some beans, until hot.
Fry the eggs in the vegetable oil for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set.
Pile the bean mixture on the tostadas, top with avocado and a fried egg, then finish with lime juice and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are firm if serving children, older adults or anyone pregnant.
Make the bean mixture ahead and reheat until steaming.

recipes.title: Lunchbox Chickpea, Corn and Herb Jar Salad
recipes.summary: A layered jar salad that stays crisp until lunch, with the dressing kept at the bottom.
steps: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, mustard and salt and divide between four jars.
Layer in the chickpeas, corn, cucumber, capsicum and spring onions, then top with the parsley and feta.
Seal and keep refrigerated until lunchtime, then shake into a bowl.
notes: Pack with an ice brick; keep chilled and eat within 4 hours out of the fridge.
Assembled jars last 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Kids' Cheesy Cauliflower Bites
recipes.summary: Soft baked cauliflower and cheese nuggets, mild enough for little ones and good cold in a lunchbox.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray with baking paper.
Steam the cauliflower for 8 minutes until very tender, then chop finely and squeeze out excess water.
Mix with the egg, cheddar and breadcrumbs until a thick mixture forms, then shape into 16 small bites.
Brush with the oil and bake for 18 minutes, turning once, until golden and firm.
notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is cooked through and the bites are hot in the centre.
Freeze uncooked bites on a tray, then bag for up to 2 months; bake from frozen for a few minutes longer.

recipes.title: Maple Carrot and Spinach Salad (Low-FODMAP Friendly)
recipes.summary: Roasted maple carrots over baby spinach with pumpkin seeds and lemon, no onion or garlic.
steps: Heat the oven to 210C and line a tray with baking paper.
Toss the carrots with 1 tbsp of the oil, 1 tbsp of the maple syrup and the salt and roast for 25 minutes until tender and caramelised.
Whisk the remaining oil, maple syrup and the lemon juice in a large bowl.
Add the spinach and warm carrots and toss until the leaves just wilt, then scatter with the pumpkin seeds.
notes: Low-FODMAP friendly: the ingredients are generally considered low in FODMAPs at these serve sizes, but individual tolerance varies, so check against your own plan.
Serve warm or cold.

recipes.title: Holiday Brunch Baked Egg Cups with Spinach and Ham
recipes.summary: Make-ahead muffin-tin egg cups with ham, spinach and cheddar, ideal for a crowd.
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and brush a 12-hole muffin tin with the butter.
Whisk the eggs, milk and pepper, then divide the ham, spinach and cheddar between the holes.
Pour in the egg mixture and bake for 20 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the centre.
notes: Food safety: bake until the eggs are fully set with no runny egg; reheat leftovers until steaming hot.
Keeps in the fridge for 3 days or freezes for 2 months.

recipes.title: Orange Cinnamon French Toast Bake for Holiday Brunch
recipes.summary: A custardy baked French toast with orange and cinnamon, prepared the night before.
steps: Grease a large baking dish with the butter and spread the bread cubes in it.
Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, orange zest and juice, cinnamon and vanilla until smooth and pour over the bread, pressing it down to soak.
Heat the oven to 180C and bake for 40 minutes until puffed, golden and the centre is set.
Serve warm with extra orange segments or yoghurt.
notes: Food safety: bake until the custard is fully set and reaches 71C in the centre.
Assemble the night before and keep covered in the fridge, then bake in the morning.
